_provenance.note: Alaska citation authorities. Alaska's SNAP regulations are cited via the Alaska Administrative Code convention '7 AAC 46.NNN' (e.g. 7 AAC 46.021, State Options), and its cross-program disqualification statute is cited via the Alaska Statutes convention 'AS 47.27.NNN' (e.g. AS 47.27.015, Disqualifying conditions). This pack defines a THIRD, non-regulatory citation family, 'akdohpdf', matching Alaska DOH's own dated PDF publications (e.g. 'FSP 77'), since this pack's most load-bearing, most-current dollar figures come from a DOH-published standards PDF rather than either the AAC or a statute, and this pack expects that citation form to appear in generated answers alongside the regulatory forms.

patterns.note: Alaska Administrative Code, Title 7 (Health and Social Services), Chapter 46 (Food Stamp Program), cited with its own subsection number, e.g. 7 AAC 46.021 (State Options), 7 AAC 46.010 (Administration of program; scope of regulations). Governs procedural/administrative options; does not itself hardcode dollar figures, which come from DOH's own annual standards PDF instead.
Alaska Statutes, cited e.g. AS 47.27.015 (Disqualifying conditions — the drug-related-felony modified-ban provision).

Alaska DOH-published SNAP standards PDF form number, e.g. FSP 77 (the 'Alaska SNAP Standards: Income Limits and Standard Deductions' publication, revision date printed on the form itself, e.g. 'rev 09/25').

akaac.note: Administration of program; scope of regulations — adopts 7 CFR 271-274 (federal SNAP regulations) by reference
State options — household-determination, verification, processing-timeline, and income-calculation options committed to state discretion; last amended 1991; does not hardcode dollar figures

akstat.note: Alaska's food stamp statute chapter (cross-referenced by AS 47.27.015's disqualification provision); this pack did not fetch AS 47.25's own full text directly

Disqualifying conditions — the modified drug-felony SNAP/TANF ban: disqualified unless the person is serving/completed probation or parole, in/completed mandatory drug or alcohol treatment, has taken rehabilitation action, or is complying with a reentry plan. Text cross-corroborated via FindLaw/Justia/CLASP secondary excerpts after a direct 403 on law.justia.com and codes.findlaw.com; not independently primary-fetched

akdohpdf.note: 'Alaska SNAP Standards: Income Limits and Standard Deductions,' rev 09/25, effective 10/1/2025 — the primary source for this pack's income-limit, deduction, allotment, and utility-allowance dollar figures
